key_insight: ArcTN finds lower-cost tensor-network contraction orders while reducing planning time, improving the efficiency of quantum circuit simulation.
engineering_relevance: Light and Heavy search presets balance planning effort against contraction cost, while slicing helps keep intermediate tensors within size limits.
method: Combine randomized-greedy construction, subtree reconfiguration, and parallel tempering.
Use stage-specific stopping rules with Light and Heavy search presets.
Apply Fixed or Dynamic slicing to meet tensor-size limits, then execute the returned orders.
evidence_signal: On 30 QC32 networks completed by all eight configurations, Light used 61.32% fewer FLOPs and planned 1.62× faster than Cotengra Auto/CMA-ES; Dynamic slicing met size limits in all 90 runs on 18 scalar-output networks.
watch_item: Dynamic slicing requires longer planning, and several reported performance comparisons include only runs completed by all compared configurations.
paper_title: ArcTN: Efficient Tensor-Network Contraction Planning for Quantum Circuit Simulation
